caption:
OpenAI's revenue jumped about 50% to $10 billion in the third quarter, CFO Sarah Friar told Yahoo Finance.
But investor documents seen by The Wall Street Journal show a $10.9 billion operating loss for the same quarter, Reuters reported.
Business customers doubled and now bring in half of OpenAI's revenue.

Will OpenAI ever make more than it spends?

site_article.headline: OpenAI revenue rises to $10 billion in third quarter as operating loss widens
site_article.dek: The company's chief financial officer called it a blockbuster quarter, while investor documents show a $10.9 billion operating loss for the same period.
site_article.summary: OpenAI's revenue grew about 50 percent from the previous quarter to roughly $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026, according to CFO Sarah Friar. Documents cited by The Wall Street Journal show its operating loss widened to $10.9 billion in the same quarter.
site_article.seo_title: OpenAI Q3 revenue hits $10 billion, operating loss $10.9 billion
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI's third quarter revenue rose about 50% to $10 billion, its CFO said, while documents show a $10.9 billion operating loss.
site_article.answer_summary: OpenAI made about $10 billion in revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up roughly 50 percent from the second quarter, but reported an operating loss of $10.9 billion, according to documents cited by The Wall Street Journal.
site_article.hero_alt: Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, photographed at an event in November 2022.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI's revenue climbed about 50 percent from the prior quarter to roughly $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026, Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar said in an interview reported by Yahoo Finance on November 10, 2026. Friar described the three months as a blockbuster quarter and said the company's annualized revenue run rate stands at about $50 billion.

The same day, Reuters reported that the growth came with steep losses. Citing The Wall Street Journal, which reviewed documents OpenAI provided to investors, Reuters said the company's operating loss widened to $10.9 billion in the third quarter from $10.1 billion in the second quarter.

Friar said OpenAI's enterprise business doubled from the second quarter, and that revenue is now split evenly between business customers and consumers. She credited products for coding and cybersecurity, along with Dots, the company's agent platform for businesses, for driving that demand.

On the consumer side, sales grew 20 percent from the previous quarter, according to Yahoo Finance. The outlet reported that OpenAI's subscriptions have passed 100 million users and that its products reach 1.2 billion weekly active users.

According to the documents cited by the Journal, OpenAI told investors that its adjusted operating margin improved to negative 109 percent, from negative 150 percent in the prior quarter. Reuters said OpenAI did not immediately respond to its request for comment.

Taken together, the figures describe a company whose sales are growing faster than its losses, yet whose operating loss for the quarter was still larger than its revenue. The margin improvement suggests costs are not rising as quickly as income, but the gap remains wide. Because OpenAI is private, these numbers come from an executive interview and investor documents rather than audited public filings, so they are harder to compare directly with a listed company.

The results surfaced as rival Anthropic began the roadshow for its initial public offering. Reuters said the share sale could value Anthropic at about $1.4 trillion. Yahoo Finance reported that Anthropic's revenue reached $33.2 billion in the nine months ended September 30, according to its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and that the listing could take place on November 19 or 20.

Friar said OpenAI had been held back by its Azure contract with Microsoft. She added that Anthropic's success with business customers showed the value of distribution agreements with outside cloud providers, and said opening up those channels could become a major tailwind for OpenAI in 2027.

The timing matters. Anthropic's offering will put detailed, audited financial statements for a leading AI developer in front of public investors, and OpenAI's own figures will inevitably be measured against them. Friar's comments frame OpenAI's slower enterprise growth in earlier quarters as partly a distribution problem rather than a product problem.
The next signal to watch is whether OpenAI announces new cloud distribution agreements beyond Microsoft, and whether its fourth quarter shows the operating loss shrinking while revenue keeps growing.
